>> This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News, I'm Charles Snyder.
Election day may be over, but votes are still being counted and results still coming in
after a blockbuster night for Democrats.
They flip key seats in the U.S. Senate and House.
NPR's Elena Moore has this update on where things stand.
So far, Democrats have flipped 29 seats in the House, according to race calls by the
Associated Press.
And more are likely, with Democratic candidates up in dozens of additional races that have
yet to be called.
On the Senate side, Democrats have flipped a whopping seven seats, with wins in Kansas,
Iowa, Maine, North Carolina, South Carolina, Texas, and Ohio.
A few tight races remain too early to call, notably Alaska and Mississippi.
Alaska was expected to be close.
It was seen as a toss-up race heading into election day.
But historically, Ruby Red, Mississippi, was not expected to be this close.
Ballots are still being counted, but the candidates are essentially tied.
Elena Moore, NPR News.
>> On Capitol Hill, New York Congressman Hakeem Jeffries is all but certain to become the
first black lawmaker to be elected Speaker of the House when that new Congress is sworn
in next year.
NPR's Eric McDaniel has this report.
As Speaker, Jeffries would be second in the presidential line of succession after the
Vice President.
He's the first black politician to lead either party in the House or Senate.
This new role would be the pinnacle of a 13-year House tenure, a rise from rank and file member
focused on criminal justice to a top party lieutenant under former Speaker Nancy Pelosi.
Now the hard part, securing buy-in from an ideologically diverse and often fractious
House Democratic caucus, as the party now looks to make good on its promises to voters.
Eric McDaniel, NPR News Washington.
>> The current speaker, Mike Johnson, is stepping down from leadership, saying Wednesday that
he will not seek reelection as House Republican leader.
Johnson is expected to stay on as a rank and file member from Louisiana when the new Congress
convenes in January.
His decision sets up an internal party battle for his replacement after Democrats swept
a power in Tuesday's midterm elections.
>> Illustrate, the Dow surged Wednesday, closing up more than 1,500 points, or more than 3%
in Paris-Raphael Naum reports.
>> There were two main reasons.
First, we did not get a contested election, which many investors had feared would lead
to volatility.
Instead, President Trump said he would accept the results.
Secondly, investors also tend to prefer divided government because they think it can prevent
potential excesses.
But it's not clear if the stock market gains will be sustained.
Democrats could pursue stronger regulations against businesses, especially when it comes
to AI and data centers.
And Elon Musk's companies, Tesla and SpaceX, tumbled after the billionaires spent hundreds
of millions of dollars trying to elect more Republicans.
Raphael Naum, NPR News.
>> And you're listening to NPR News.
President Trump says he is not considering replacing Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
But he is acknowledging the Iran war's impact on his party's losses in the midterm elections.
His remarks came after Vice President J.D. Vance publicly broke with Trump, posting a
lengthy social media post saying the war was the reason voters rejected the GOP.
Food conglomerate Kraft Heinz says it's selling off its coffee business in North America,
which includes Maxwell House.
The company hopes the move will help boost growth, as NPR's Elena Seljuk reports.
Kraft Heinz has been on deal watch for a while, ever since its CEO earlier this year hit pause
on a massive breakup the company had planned.
Kraft Heinz had been losing sales and at one point proposed as a solution to undo its historic
merger and split Kraft away from Heinz, dividing faster-growing sauces and condiments from
slower-growing groceries.
But new CEO Steve K. Helene said the real issue was the company under-investing in its
brands.
Now, he's hoping to jump-start growth, in part by selling the majority ownership of
its North American coffee business to a private equity firm called One Rock Capital Partners.
The company did not say how Maxwell or other brands might change.
Elena Seljuk, NPR News.
NASA's Space Telescope met a fiery end Wednesday.
The SWIFT satellite telescope fell out of orbit, as expected.
NASA says it burned up in the Earth's atmosphere over Indonesia.
The SWIFT telescope was launched more than 20 years ago.
Its demise came less than three months after a rescue spacecraft failed in its mission
to extend the scope's life by boosting it to a higher orbit.

Hakeem Jeffries poised to become first Black Speaker of the House when new Congress convenes

Dow surges more than 1,500 points after midterms pass without contested election, Musk's Tesla and SpaceX fall
